hero.description: A photo carousel where the name, description and link on each tile are all optional.

bare.title: Photos only
bare.description: No name, description or link. This is what a site renders when it cannot name the animals in its own photos -- inventing a name is not an option.

linked.title: Named, described and linked
linked.description: Every optional field set. The first two tiles deliberately point at the same anchor, because one story often has more than one photo.

anchors.one: Anchor target one -- the first two tiles link here.
anchors.two: Anchor target two -- the last two tiles link here.

standard.title: Standard
items: Use `MediaCarouselSection` instead of a page-local photo carousel.
`name`, `description` and `href` are all optional and independent -- a tile with none of them renders as a bare photo.
Several tiles may share one `href`; one story often has more than one photo.
The page owns the heading, not the module -- this keeps heading levels correct and lets the carousel sit under whatever `<h2>` the page already has.
Photos are never cropped: tiles are `aspect-[3/4]` with `object-contain`, so the whole image is always visible.
`href` passes through `safeContentUrl`; a disallowed scheme renders the tile unlinked rather than dropping it.
Anchor targets need a `scroll-mt-*` matching the site's sticky header, or the target lands underneath it.
Leave `autoPlayDelayMs` unset once tiles are links -- an auto-advancing carousel slides the link out from under the pointer.
A video tile links from its caption only; wrapping `<video controls>` in an anchor would navigate on play.
